title: Skills
text:
# Skills

> Discover and read Agent Skills from MCP servers

The ext-skills repository
contains the published specification for the official Skills extension
(`io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`). SEP-2640 is Final.

The Skills Over MCP Working Group
maintains the extension. SDK and host support is still being implemented;
see the client support matrix and
implementations list
for current coverage.

> [card] modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills
> 
> Specification and documentation for Skills over MCP.

The Skills extension allows MCP servers to expose workflow instructions and
supporting files to clients. Clients can discover available skills, retrieve
their metadata, and read their contents using the existing Resources primitive.

A skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file and optional supporting
files, following the Agent Skills specification.
This extension defines discovery and retrieval over MCP.

Skills are useful for reusable workflows that combine several tools or require
supporting references, such as code review or document processing. Serving them
over MCP keeps those instructions with the service they describe. Clients can
discover available workflows from metadata and load instructions and supporting
files only when needed.

...

title: Extension Support Matrix
text:
# Extension Support Matrix

> Which MCP clients implement which official extensions

This matrix shows which MCP clients support each official extension. Extensions are always opt-in: a client only uses an extension if both client and server declare support in the `extensions` field of their capabilities.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> This list is maintained by the community. If you notice any inaccuracies or would like to add or update information, please submit a pull request.

## Extension overview

| Extension | Identifier | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP Apps | `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` | Interactive HTML interfaces rendered inline in the conversation |
| OAuth Client Credentials | `io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials` | Machine-to-machine auth without interactive user login |
| Enterprise-Managed Authorization | `io.modelcontextprotocol/enterprise-managed-authorization` | Centralized access control via enterprise IdP |
| Skills over MCP | `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` | Discover skills and read their instructions and supporting files |

title: Three clients support Skills over MCP, all marked Partial. | MindPattern
text:
The newly published extension support matrix shows exactly three entries in the Skills column: ChatGPT (importing skills from an MCP server), fast-agent, and MCP Inspector (verification via its CLI `--verify`). Claude web, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot and Goose all show MCP Apps support and nothing in Skills. Shipping skills over MCP instead of on disk today means one consumer product, one framework, one debugging tool.

title: How to Load Agent Skills from an MCP Server (SEP-2640)
text:
You can load agent skills from an MCP server today only if your client supports MCP's Skills extension, defined in SEP-2640, and as of Oct 30, 2026 that is still a short list. The MCP project's support matrix shows partial Skills support in ChatGPT, fast-agent and MCP Inspector. The ext-skills implementations list adds a few more developer tools, such as MCPJam Inspector and the mcpc CLI. The matrix lists no Skills support for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code GitHub Copilot, and Codex is not on it at all, so in those tools skills still come from folders on disk or from plugins. The MCP project's own page says SDK and host support is still being implemented, so expect this list to change. This guide is for people who use skills, not people who build servers: what the extension does from your side, the steps where it works, and what to do where it doesn't.

...

## Why answers to this question disagree

Search for "agent skills MCP server" and you get three different things under the same words.

1. The official Skills extension. The server lists its skills, and a supporting client fetches a skill's SKILL.md and files when a task needs them. This is SEP-2640, extension ID io.modelcontextprotocol/skills. It needs support in your client.

2. Skills served as MCP prompts. Some servers expose each skill as an MCP prompt. Any client that shows MCP prompts can run them, but a prompt is a single block of text, without a skill's folder of scripts and reference files.

title: Delivering Agent Skills Over MCP | Microsoft Community Hub
text:
The official Skills extension for Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standard way to make skills available from a server, so compatible agents can find and load them when needed.

...

MCP already gives agents access to content from servers through resources. The Skills extension builds on that. It adds a way to ask which skills a server offers and get the details needed to load them.

It doesn't change the skill format, and it doesn't run a skill on the server. The application running your agent, called the host, still decides how to offer skills to the user or model and load the selected instructions.

Both the server and the host need the right support. Being able to call an MCP tool isn't enough to discover and load remote skills. A custom tool that returns skill text isn't, by itself, an implementation of this extension either.

The extension is identified as `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills`. Its proposal, SEP-2640, has reached Final status. Client support is still developing, so a published specification doesn't mean every MCP host supports it yet.

...

## Where Microsoft Foundry fits

Microsoft Foundry offers skills support in preview. Its integration guide describes toolbox-based skill discovery as following SEP-2640.

A toolbox gives agents one MCP endpoint for accessing its tools and skills. To share a skill this way:

1. Upload the skill content to create a skill version in your Foundry project.

title: skills - MCP Python SDK
text:
# skills

Client-side Skills extension (SEP-2640).

`Skills` is an opt-in `ClientExtension` for talking to a skills catalog server. Register it with `Client(extensions=[Skills()])`, then call `client.extension(Skills)` for the SEP-2640 verbs — `list_skills`, `get_skill`, and `read_directory` — tied to that connection:

```
async with Client("http://localhost:8000/mcp", extensions=[Skills()]) as client:
    for skill in await client.extension(Skills).list_skills():
        print(skill.uri, skill.frontmatter["description"])

```

`client.extension(Skills)` returns a `SkillsClient`. Its catalog verbs — `list_skills`, `get_skill`, and `read_directory` — check that the server advertises the extension and validate its response; `list_skills` and `read_directory` follow `nextCursor` to completion, so one call returns every page's results.

title: Skills Over MCP Working Group - April 21st 2026 Office Hours Notes · modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol · Discussion #2628 · GitHub
text:
Ola opened with results from a survey of open-source MCP clients that already expose a model-facing `read_resource` tool, which the draft Skills Extension SEP (#69) relies on. Four clients were tested with light forks: fast-agent, Gemini CLI, Codex, and Goose — all four already support both a read-resource tool and file-based skills, so the modding only added the connective tissue from the SEP (skill-resource indexing alongside the regular resource index; contextual server-name hinting).
